key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, increasing laser power deepens penetration, increasing travel speed reduces weld dimensions, and increasing current widens the weld and stabilizes the arc.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide weld penetration, bead geometry, and arc-stability control when fabricating Invar molds for aerospace composites.
method: Parameter studies of laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports trends over 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min welding speed, and 150–170 A current, but provides no quantitative validation metrics.
watch_item: Apply the findings cautiously outside the studied parameter ranges; higher power and speed can also promote arc deflection or deformation.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
